subproblem.title: Finite partial sums of integer multiplicity currents are integer multiplicity, with subadditive mass (parent steps 1–2)
subproblem.statement:
Let P, n ∈ ℕ and U ⊆ ℝ^P. Assume (IS_U): for all integer multiplicity A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U), the current A − B is integer multiplicity. Let Y_i ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (i ∈ ℕ) all be integer multiplicity. Then for every N ∈ ℕ there is an integer multiplicity Z ∈ 𝒟_n(U) such that:
- Z(ω) = Σ_{i=0}^{N} Y_i(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), and
- M_G(Z) ≤ Σ_{i=0}^{N} M_G(Y_i) in [0, ∞] for every set G ⊆ ℝ^P.

Conventions:
- 𝒟_n(U) = SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn U n, and 𝒟^n(U) = TestFormOn U n is the space of test n-forms in U.
- Integer multiplicity is the contract predicate IsIntegerMultiplicity.
- A − B is the contract subtraction (instance Sub), which acts by (A − B)(ω) = A(ω) − B(ω).
- M_G(T) = T.massOn G is the supremum in [0, ∞] of ENNReal.ofReal(T(ω)) over ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for all x.
- Σ_{i=0}^{N} denotes the sum over Finset.range (N + 1).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (Y : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U n), (∀ A B : GeometricCurrentOn U n, IsIntegerMultiplicity A → IsIntegerMultiplicity B → IsIntegerMultiplicity (A - B)) → (∀ i, IsIntegerMultiplicity (Y i)) → ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ Z : GeometricCurrentOn U n, IsIntegerMultiplicity Z ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Z ω = ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), Y i ω) ∧ ∀ G : Set (Euclid P), Z.massOn G ≤ ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (N + 1), (Y i).massOn G
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1–2 of the parent proof. These define the sum A ⊕ B := A − ((B − B) − B), show it is integer multiplicity (IM) by (IS), and build the partial sums R^N, S^N by iterating ⊕.

Fix P, n, U and the family (Y_i). Assume (IS_U) and that every Y_i is IM.
The contract subtraction acts pointwise: its underlying functional is the difference of the two functionals. So (A − B)(ω) = A(ω) − B(ω) for all A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U); this holds by definition.
Write Σ_{i=0}^{N} for the sum over Finset.range (N + 1).
We prove the following claim C(N) by induction on N: there is an IM Z ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with Z(ω) = Σ_{i=0}^{N} Y_i(ω) for all ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), and M_G(Z) ≤ Σ_{i=0}^{N} M_G(Y_i) for all G ⊆ ℝ^P.

1. (Base case N = 0.) Take Z := Y_0. It is IM by hypothesis. For every ω, Σ_{i=0}^{0} Y_i(ω) = Y_0(ω) = Z(ω). For every G, Σ_{i=0}^{0} M_G(Y_i) = M_G(Y_0) = M_G(Z), so the mass inequality holds with equality.
2. (Inductive step: set-up.) Assume C(N), witnessed by Z. Put B := Y_{N+1} and Z' := Z − ((B − B) − B) ∈ 𝒟_n(U).
3. (Z' is IM.)
   B is IM, so B − B is IM by (IS_U) applied to B and B.
   Then (B − B) − B is IM by (IS_U) applied to the IM currents B − B and B.
   Finally Z' = Z − ((B − B) − B) is IM by (IS_U) applied to the IM currents Z and (B − B) − B.
4. (Evaluation of Z'.) For every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), the pointwise action of subtraction gives Z'(ω) = Z(ω) − ((B(ω) − B(ω)) − B(ω)) = Z(ω) + B(ω). By C(N), Z(ω) = Σ_{i=0}^{N} Y_i(ω), so Z'(ω) = Σ_{i=0}^{N} Y_i(ω) + Y_{N+1}(ω) = Σ_{i=0}^{N+1} Y_i(ω) (Finset.sum_range_succ).
5. (Mass of Z'.) Fix G ⊆ ℝ^P.
   By step 4, Z'(ω) = Z(ω) + 1·B(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), in particular for every ω with tsupport ω ⊆ G.
   Apply the sibling mass_triangle (Submission.cmc_fc_sl_massOn_le_add_of_eval_eq) with the sets U and G, the currents Z in the role of X, B in the role of Y and Z' in the role of Z, and the scalar c = 1 (|1| ≤ 1). It gives M_G(Z') ≤ M_G(Z) + M_G(B).
   By C(N), M_G(Z) ≤ Σ_{i=0}^{N} M_G(Y_i). By monotonicity of addition in [0, ∞], M_G(Z') ≤ Σ_{i=0}^{N} M_G(Y_i) + M_G(Y_{N+1}) = Σ_{i=0}^{N+1} M_G(Y_i) (Finset.sum_range_succ).
6. (Conclusion.) Steps 3–5 show that Z' witnesses C(N + 1). By induction C(N) holds for every N ∈ ℕ, which is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: Induction on N, with base case Z := Y_0.
Inductive step: Z' := Z − ((B − B) − B) with B := Y_{N+1}; three applications of (IS_U) show Z' is integer multiplicity.
Pointwise subtraction gives Z'(ω) = Z(ω) + B(ω) = Σ_{i=0}^{N+1} Y_i(ω) (Finset.sum_range_succ).
Sibling mass_triangle with c = 1, plus the induction hypothesis, gives M_G(Z') ≤ Σ_{i=0}^{N+1} M_G(Y_i).

audit.reason: The one-line proposition exactly states the inclusive partial sum and a single witness satisfying every evaluation and local-mass bound. The base case and induction are complete: three valid applications of IS_U establish integer multiplicity, contract subtraction gives addition on evaluations, and mass_triangle at c = 1 supplies the mass estimate. Openness is unnecessary because subtraction closure is an explicit hypothesis. Its sole child dependency is correctly declared and non-circular. Choosing these witnesses supplies the partial-sum sequences needed by the selected parent.
